_comment: Single source of truth for MCP servers across Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini/Antigravity. Edit here, then run: mcp-sync. Each tool stores MCP config in a different file and a different schema; mcp-sync translates. GitHub Copilot is not part of this ecosystem and is never written to. Being listed here is NOT a grant: an entry says how FDE would run a server, never that anyone may. Readiness, profile, stage and role decide that, and `fde mcp status` shows the result.
_targets: Every server declares who gets it. 'claude' | 'gemini' | 'codex' are global targets, written into each CLI's user-level config. 'role:<role>' is a run-scoped target: the server is NOT placed in anyone's global config, and mcp-sync --run <run-id> writes it only for the identity that holds that role in that run. A server is one or the other, never both.
_secrets: No credential is ever written here. A userConfig field with "secret": true names an environment variable; the value lives in ~/.claude-shared/secrets/mcp/<server>/<field> with mode 0600 and is injected only into the child process that needs it.

coding.label: Coding
coding.description: Repository work: semantic navigation and version-accurate library documentation.

frontend-testing.label: Frontend testing
frontend-testing.description: Browser workflows, accessibility evidence and front-end root-cause analysis.

client-delivery.label: Acme delivery
client-delivery.description: Requirements, delivery traceability and design context for client engagements.

data.label: Data
data.description: Schema discovery and bounded read-only SQL against an explicitly selected database.

observability.label: Observability
observability.description: Traces, prompts, evaluations and cloud operational evidence.

context7.useWhen: You need version-specific external documentation: a framework, dependency, SDK or public API whose behaviour changes between releases.
preferOver: a web search for API signatures
context7.doNotUseWhen: The question is about this repository, its conventions or its own code — read the repository instead.
context7.note: Up-to-date library and framework docs. Read-only, no tenant data, safe for every identity. When it is active it is the source for version-sensitive API facts; recalled documentation is not.

mutationApproval.note: Serena's edits would land in the repository, not outside this machine, so they belong behind the run's existing one-time Codex write approval — not behind a publication approval. Until such a scope is authorised, its editing tools are simply absent.

serena.useWhen: Symbol lookup, finding references, dependency-aware navigation of unfamiliar code, and semantic refactoring targets.
preferOver: reading a whole file to find one definition
serena.doNotUseWhen: A small, direct read of a known file, or a generated / non-code file — the ordinary filesystem tools are cheaper and clearer there.
serena.note: Semantic code navigation over LSP. FDE never installs it: it is detected, and the exact setup command is shown when it is absent. Its editing tools are denied here; an implementation write still goes through the run's own approval, not through this server.

requires.setup: Node.js provides npx. The pinned package is fetched on first use, never when a page is opened.

package.name: @playwright/mcp
package.update: change the pinned version in mcp-servers.json, then: mcp-sync

userConfig.name: outputDir
userConfig.label: Output directory
userConfig.placeholder: leave blank for a temporary directory

playwright.useWhen: Browser workflows, accessibility-tree interaction, responsive behaviour and end-to-end verification of a UI you are building.
playwright.doNotUseWhen: A repeatable acceptance check belongs in the repository's own Playwright tests — write the test rather than driving the browser once. Do not activate it alongside Chrome DevTools unless the task needs both.
playwright.note: Isolated, headless sessions by default: no profile is saved to disk and no signed-in browser is reused. Arbitrary script evaluation, file upload and installation tools are denied. A browser action that submits, publishes, purchases, sends or otherwise mutates an external authenticated service is an external mutation and needs the matching fde approve-publish first.

requires.setup: Node.js provides npx. The pinned package is fetched on first use, never when a page is opened.

package.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
package.update: change the pinned version in mcp-servers.json, then: mcp-sync

userConfig.name: slim
userConfig.label: Slim mode (three basic tools only)
userConfig.help: Verified against 1.9.0: --slim exposes only evaluate, navigate and screenshot, so the console, network and performance tools this server exists for are absent. FDE therefore runs it non-slim by default and controls scope with a verified tool allowlist instead, which is a stricter limit than --slim, not a looser one.

userConfig.name: browserUrl
userConfig.label: Attach to an already running browser (advanced)
userConfig.placeholder: leave blank — see the warning below
userConfig.warning: Attaching gives this server your live browser session, including anything you are signed in to. FDE never does this on its own; set it only for a debugging session you are watching, and clear it afterwards.

mutationApproval.note: This server's interaction and script-evaluation tools are denied outright in this phase, by any approval. Driving a page is Playwright's job, under Playwright's own origin restrictions.

chrome-devtools.useWhen: Front-end debugging: console errors, network waterfalls and failed requests, runtime state and performance traces — the root cause behind a symptom.
preferOver: guessing at a cause from a stack trace alone
chrome-devtools.doNotUseWhen: You need to drive a user flow — that is Playwright's job. Do not activate both unless the task genuinely needs interaction and deep diagnostics.
chrome-devtools.note: Runs headless and isolated. It never attaches to your normal signed-in Chrome profile automatically; connecting to an existing browser is an explicit, warned, operator-set option. Its interaction tools are denied so the Playwright/DevTools division of labour is enforced, not merely suggested.

userConfig.name: allowTools
userConfig.label: Pin a read-only tool allowlist (comma separated)
userConfig.placeholder: leave blank until you know this provider's read tool names
userConfig.help: FDE cannot ask this server what tools it has, because the OAuth token belongs to the MCP client. Until you pin a list here, the server reaches a session with every tool it offers and its writes are governed by fde approve-publish alone. Pinning turns this into an enforced allowlist.

atlassian.useWhen: Requirements, Jira issues, Confluence pages and delivery traceability, after the combined plan and roles are approved.
preferOver: asking the operator to paste an issue description
guessing at a ticket's current state
atlassian.doNotUseWhen: Before plan approval, or for repository files — Rovo does not provide unrestricted Bitbucket repository operations; use local git or the Bitbucket REST connection.
atlassian.note: Jira and Confluence through Atlassian Rovo MCP v2. Deliberately not global: there is no permanently privileged orchestrator account, so this reaches whichever identity the user made orchestrator for the run, and only after roles are confirmed. Reads are allowed then; writes still need fde approve-publish. Bitbucket remains a separate REST or local-git connection.

userConfig.name: allowTools
userConfig.label: Pin a read-only tool allowlist (comma separated)
userConfig.placeholder: leave blank until you know this provider's read tool names
userConfig.help: FDE cannot ask this server what tools it has, because the OAuth token belongs to the MCP client. Until you pin a list here, the server reaches a session with every tool it offers and its writes are governed by fde approve-publish alone. Pinning turns this into an enforced allowlist.

figma.useWhen: A design stage needs the real design context: variables, components, tokens and frame structure for design-to-code.
preferOver: reimplementing spacing and colour from a screenshot
figma.doNotUseWhen: The run has no design stage, or the question is answerable from the design system documentation already in the repository.
figma.note: Official remote Figma MCP server. Run-scoped to the selected UI/UX designer after plan approval; OAuth remains in that provider's MCP client. Reading is allowed within the approved plan. Any canvas write or transfer of a reconciled design requires fde approve-publish <run-id> figma. The isolated design-panel runner still disables tools, so panel participants produce governed proposals rather than racing on one canvas.

requires.setup: Node.js provides npx. Configure a dedicated read-only database account first; FDE will not create one.

package.name: @bytebase/dbhub
package.update: change the pinned version in mcp-servers.json, then: mcp-sync

userConfig.name: readOnlyAccount
userConfig.label: The database account itself is read-only
userConfig.help: DBHub's read-only mode is one of two layers. FDE will not activate this server until you confirm the database account cannot write either.

generatedFiles.template:
# Generated by FDE. Do not edit: rewritten by `fde mcp configure dbhub`.
# The DSN is an environment reference, never a value. DBHub interpolates
# ${VAR} at startup from the environment FDE injects into its child process.

[[sources]]
id = "default"
dsn = "${FDE_MCP_DBHUB_DSN}"

[[tools]]
name = "execute_sql"
source = "default"
readonly = true
max_rows = {{config.maxRows}}
query_timeout_seconds = {{config.queryTimeoutSeconds}}

dbhub.useWhen: Schema discovery, table and index metadata, query planning, and bounded SELECT statements against a database the operator explicitly selected.
preferOver: guessing a schema from ORM models
asking the operator to paste a table definition
dbhub.doNotUseWhen: The run has not selected the data profile, or the question is about application code rather than stored data. Write SQL is not implemented in this phase at all.
dbhub.note: PostgreSQL only for now. Read-only is enforced twice: DBHub's own execute_sql readonly mode in the generated TOML, and a database account that has SELECT and nothing else — FDE refuses to activate until you confirm the second. Rows are capped at the configured maximum and queries at the configured timeout.

requires.setup: Install the AWS CLI and sign in with `aws sso login --profile <profile>` (or configure credentials). FDE never copies AWS credentials into its own metadata.

package.name: mcp-proxy-for-aws-cli
package.update: change the pinned version in mcp-servers.json, then: mcp-sync

userConfig.name: expectedAccountId
userConfig.label: Expected account id (optional)
userConfig.placeholder: verification fails loudly if the caller is someone else

aws.useWhen: Cloud architecture questions, inventory and discovery, release evidence and operational investigation on AWS.
preferOver: shelling out to the aws CLI ad hoc
aws.doNotUseWhen: The run is not doing solutioning, release management, observability or AWS-specific research. Do not reach for a specialised AWS Labs server until a concrete run needs that capability.
aws.note: Runs the official proxy with --read-only, so write tools are absent from the process rather than merely discouraged. Authentication uses the local AWS credential chain; FDE stores no AWS credential and shows account, role and region without exposing one. Creating, modifying, deleting or deploying anything, or any cost-bearing action, requires fde approve-publish <run-id> deployment and is recorded.

requires.setup: Install the Azure CLI (`brew install azure-cli`) and run `az login`. FDE never installs it and never stores an Azure credential.

package.name: @azure/mcp
package.update: change the pinned version in mcp-servers.json, then: mcp-sync

userConfig.name: namespaces
userConfig.label: Allowed namespaces (comma separated)
userConfig.help: Start narrow. Every namespace you add multiplies the tool count the model has to reason about.

azure.useWhen: Azure and Foundry tasks: resource inventory, monitor queries, architecture and operational evidence.
preferOver: reciting Azure resource names from memory
azure.doNotUseWhen: The task is not Azure-specific. Do not widen the namespace list to explore.
azure.note: The maintained microsoft/mcp Azure server, not the archived Azure/azure-mcp. Starts in namespace mode with only the namespaces you allow, and with --read-only. Authentication is the local Azure CLI identity. Resource changes and deployments require fde approve-publish <run-id> deployment.

requires.setup: Create a project API key pair in Langfuse, then paste the public and secret keys here. FDE composes the Basic credential at launch and never stores the composed header.

userConfig.name: endpoint
userConfig.label: MCP endpoint
userConfig.help: Cloud: https://<region host>/api/public/mcp. Self-hosted: your own HTTPS host with the same path. Local development may use http://localhost:3000/api/public/mcp.

langfuse.useWhen: Agent observability: traces, sessions, prompt versions, evaluation results and scores when investigating how a run or an agent actually behaved.
preferOver: reasoning about an agent failure from its final output alone
langfuse.doNotUseWhen: The project does not use Langfuse, or the question is about local FDE run events — those are in the run's own events.jsonl.
langfuse.note: Langfuse exposes prompt-creation and other write tools by default, so this entry is activated only once `fde mcp verify langfuse` has listed its tools and an enforceable read-only subset exists. If none does, the server stays blocked and says so rather than being described as read-only. Keys are project-scoped; the composed Authorization header exists only in the child process.
